subject: Caretix discovery — ops & perf alignment (post-call)
messages:
From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@caretix.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Caretix discovery — ops & perf alignment (post-call)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Samira and Mark — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the ops constraints you called out, and proposed next steps so we can size a focused PoC. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of pain / goals
- Primary goal: integrate a low-latency question-answering layer into Caretix Support chat for real-time assistance to agents (goal: reduce handle time by ~20%).
- Traffic profile (from you): steady-state ~35 RPS with 5–10% spikes up to 80 RPS during incident windows; median prompt length ~120 tokens, expected response ~80–150 tokens.
- Perf targets (your asks): p50 generation latency <= 80 ms; p95 generation latency <= 250 ms; end-to-end (API->UI visible) target p95 <= 350 ms.
- Accuracy / model quality: preference for open models in the 13B–70B range with instruction tuning; you mentioned acceptable quality at 13B if ranking/reranking used.
- Security & compliance: Caretix must maintain logs for 2 years, customer data must remain in US datacenter, and SOC2 attestation required (you'll share the security questionnaire).

Operational constraints we discussed
- Prefer Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput; fallback to Hosted in other regions acceptable for DR.
- KV-cache warm-up matters for first-token latency on conversational flows; you have sessions with frequent context reuse.
- Procurement window: Q1 purchase decision; legal prefers single SOW with usage-based overage caps.

Technical approach we propose
- Topology recommendation (initial PoC): Redwood Dedicated capacity in us-west with 2x 80GB A100 GPUs behind a per-tenant routing tier; model variant: Llama-3-13B-int8 as baseline, fallback to Llama-3-7B-quantized for cost-sensitive routes.
- Batching + latency: dynamic, small-window batching with target batch sizes 4–12 depending on concurrency to keep p95 within target while preserving token cost.
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for agent sessions; pre-warm strategy during session start to avoid cold-token spikes.
- Safety/fallback: we’ll configure model variant routing and graceful degrade to CPU-backed embeddings-only responses for extreme load.

Data we need from you to scope PoC
1) Representative sample of 500–1,000 anonymized prompts (we only need content/length distribution, not PII).
2) Expected concurrency distribution per minute for a typical day and a peak day.
3) Access to your security questionnaire (SOC2 + data residency/retention clauses).

Next steps (recommended timeline)
- Dec 17: Redwood shares a one-page PoC SOW & bench plan (I’ll attach).
- Dec 22: Caretix shares prompt samples + questionnaire.
- Jan 4–18: PoC run — ingest sample set, run latency/throughput sweeps, provide p50/p95 & cost estimates.

Attachments: caretix_perf_snapshot.csv (sample CSV schema we’ll accept), sample Redwood Dedicated topology diagram.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Karthik and Marissa on the PoC bench config and send the SOW by EOD 12/17.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@caretix.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Cc: Mark Thompson <mark@caretix.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Caretix discovery — ops & perf alignment (post-call)

Thanks Priyom — this is a helpful write-up and captures the key pieces. A few clarifications:
- The 35 RPS steady-state is per-region; our primary US region is busiest. Global traffic is small for now.
- For p95 targets you quoted, the 350 ms end-to-end is strict because our UI adds ~80–100 ms render time. So backend (generation) p95 target of 250 ms is non-negotiable for our product promise.
- Model note: we’ll start with a 13B family if you can show comparable QA accuracy to our current 30B baseline on our evaluation prompts (we’ll share the eval set).

We’ll pull the anonymized prompt set (legal is ok with stripping IDs) and the SOC2 questionnaire. I’ll loop in contracts@caretix.ai for SOW review once you send it.

Can you also include a quick estimate of committed monthly spend for the Dedicated config you proposed so we can budget? If you can give a delta for 13B int8 vs 7B quant, that’d be great.

Samira
Head of Product, Caretix

Attachments: n/a
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: internal: perf knobs and bench plan for Caretix PoC

Quick internal note following Samira’s ask — bench plan items I’m proposing so the SOW is tight: 
1) Bench targets: run synthetic traffic sweeps at 10/25/50/80 RPS; measure generation-only p50/p95 and end-to-end simulated p95 (add 100 ms front-end render).
2) Model candidates: Llama-3-13B-int8 (baseline), Mistral-7B-quant (fallback), and a 30B eval run to validate quality delta (run fewer tokens).
3) GPU profile: 2x80GB A100 should sustain 50 RPS for 13B int8 with batching 8 and token length 200 — call out: for sustained 80 RPS we need either burst capacity or a 3rd GPU in Dedicated pool.
4) KV-cache & prefixing: include a warm-up test where 25% of sessions have an identical 32-token prefix to gauge cache hit improvement on first-token latency.
5) Cost delta: estimate 13B int8 will be ~40% cheaper than 30B baseline at similar quality with reranking; 7B quant ~35% cheaper than 13B on GPU-hours but worse quality on long-context multi-turn.

I’ll draft a bench config and cost grid for Priyom to attach to the SOW. Note to Priyom: flag that Caretix asked for 2-year retention — we should include a note about long-term storage costs and log-export retention buckets in the SOW.

Karthik
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@caretix.ai>, Mark Thompson <mark@caretix.ai>, contracts@caretix.ai

Subject: Caretix PoC SOW + bench plan (next steps & asks)

Hi Samira/Mark — attaching the one-page PoC SOW and the bench configuration spreadsheet (attached as caretix_perf_snapshot.csv). Highlights and immediate asks: 
- SOW highlights: 3-week PoC, Redwood Dedicated in us-west, throughput sweeps at 10/25/50/80 RPS, and a quality check against your eval set. We include two reserved A100 GPUs for baseline and 1-week burst capacity to simulate 80 RPS sustained.
- Budget ballpark (committed monthly): approx $37k/mo for the reserved Dedicated footprint we sketched (2x80GB A100, managed infra, monitoring), delta to add a 3rd GPU for sustained 80 RPS: +$12k/mo. Estimates include monitoring & 2-year log retention export to S3 (billing estimate separate).
- Data & artifacts we need from Caretix to start: prompt sample (500–1k), eval set for QA, completed SOC2 questionnaire, PO or signature from contracts@caretix.ai to start provisioning.

Next actions I’ll take by EOD Mon (12/20):
- Send the SOW PDF + bench CSV (attached).
- Kick off internal capacity reservation request (ops) contingent on PO.

Samira — once you confirm timing for sharing the prompt/eval artifacts we’ll slot the bench run and reserve the GPUs. If contracts want a short call to review the SOW language I can hop on.

Best,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
